- Model consistently underestimates true price movements, especially after sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment > 0.75 → forecast lags and misses upward swings).
- When sentiment turns negative (e.g., < 0.5), model fails to anticipate sharp downward corrections; forecast remains flat or slightly upward.
- After a price spike (e.g., >75), model overcorrects with a steep downward slope, then fails to recover — overshoot followed by mean reversion.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward lower prices; model doesn’t adjust for recent volatility or sentiment-driven momentum.
- If sentiment is high and price is rising, model underreacts — fails to capture momentum; if sentiment drops, model overreacts to downward pressure.
- Model exhibits “flatline” behavior in early forecast days (e.g., first 5–7 days) — ignores recent sentiment shifts and historical volatility.
- When sentiment is high and price is low, model tends to overcorrect upward — creates false “recovery” signals that don’t materialize.
- Correction: adjust forecast slope upward if sentiment > 0.75 and price is below recent 10-day average; adjust downward if sentiment < 0.4 and price is above 10-day average.
